headline: 🔑 THE 7/25 'YES' ON 355 COMANCHE FINALLY HAS A NAME, AND IT IS THE OFFER YOU CONFIRMED DEAD THIS MORNING — Cassie C. at RE/MAX Advantage wrote 'Writing up an offer!' on her feedback form, called $299,000 too high, and has never been told the price came down to $295,000 three days later. Second anonymous row identified on this listing today, and the warmer of the two.

hotSignals.signal: Cassie C. at RE/MAX Advantage answered 'interested: Yes' and wrote "Writing up an offer!" on her form, while calling $299,000 too high — and that is the offer confirmed dead this morning, from a buyer who was never told the price came down to $295,000.
hotSignals.action: CALL HER — thank her for showing, tell her the number her client called too high is now $295,000, and ask what gets their buyer in the house. Quote $295,000 and nothing else. No email — a buyer's agent on a live listing is a call, not a message.

hotSignals.signal: Angela B. at Keller Williams Vestavia filed the listing's other 'interested: Yes', objecting only to the price at $299,000 and noting her buyer had seen another home she liked.
hotSignals.action: Call her — the price objection has already been answered by the 8/5 reduction and she was never told. Six days on, the cross-shopped house is either under contract or not, and one call settles it. Quote $295,000 only.

hotSignals.signal: Mallory W. at ARC Realty filed the only unqualified 'interested: Yes / priced just right' this board has ever taken.
hotSignals.action: The agent call is cleared. The open item is the seller decision behind it — one call covers this seller's three files.

upcoming: 📅 SUN 8/9 · 1:30 PM — 355 COMANCHE ST, Montevallo. ⭐ Booked Friday night and still the newest thing on this board. It lands the day before the appointment you were already counting on.

⭐ ALSO WORTH KNOWING: a teammate's buyer asked to see 355 Comanche and is working on pre-approval. Not booked in the system, so it will not appear here until it is.

feedback.note: 🔴 THE READ YOU WAITED ALL WEEK FOR, filed 3:13 PM Friday off Thursday's 11:00 AM tour — the first fresh booking since the price cut. Interested: NO. Staging 3 of 5. ⛔ THE DECISIVE PART IS THE BLANKS: 'is it priced right' — blank. 'price change recommendation' — blank. 'what price' — blank. 'main thing' — blank. An agent who thinks a house is overpriced usually says so; this one declined to say anything at all.

🔎 THE ANONYMOUS ROW, NAMED THIS MORNING. Interested: YES. Priced TOO HIGH against the $299,000 list. Staging 4 of 5 — the best staging score this listing has ever taken, and it undercuts the theory that presentation is the whole problem. ⭐ HER FREE TEXT IS THE PART THAT MATTERS: "Saw another home that she is interested in." That is a cross-shopping buyer, not a rejection — and her price objection was answered three days later by the cut to $295,000, which she was never told about. ⚠️ Like every other agent on this file, she left 'what price' blank.

🔑 IDENTIFIED THIS RUN AFTER FOURTEEN DAYS AS AN ANONYMOUS ROW — and it is the origin of the offer. Interested: YES. Priced right: TOO HIGH, filed while the list was still $299,000. Replacement price: she left it blank. Main thing: "Writing up an offer!" ⭐ THAT OFFER IS THE ONE CONFIRMED DEAD AT 8:18 THIS MORNING — which means her buyer wrote once, objected to a number that has since come down $4,000, and was never told. ⚠️ Fourteen days is long enough for that buyer to be under contract elsewhere; this is a re-open, not a live offer.

listings.note: 🆕 THE PRICE POST IS UNBLOCKED. The marketing engine had been holding the 'price improved to $295,000' announcement since Wednesday, waiting on one answer: is the 7/25 offer dead? You answered at 8:18 this morning — dead. ⭐ AND THIS RUN FOUND WHERE THAT OFFER CAME FROM: the 7/25 feedback, anonymous on this board for two weeks, was Cassie C. at RE/MAX Advantage writing "Writing up an offer!" ⛔ QUOTE $295,000 AND NOTHING ELSE on both agent calls — across five written reads and one preview, not one agent has ever put a different number on paper. ⭐ Two showings booked this weekend on a listing where one booking had been news.

feedback.note: 🔥 NOT A FEEDBACK FORM — A DEAL. At 9:05 Friday morning he wrote that the buyers agree to ALL of the counter's new terms with one exception: they want to close on or before Oct 23 rather than Oct 30, because they have four kids and moving the week of Halloween will not work. ⭐ Price agreed. Concession agreed. Co-op agreed. Appliances agreed. ⚠️ HE THEN CHASED IT HIMSELF at 2:51 PM — "any update on the closing date ask?" ⏰ AS OF THIS MORNING THE ANSWER IS ABOUT 22 HOURS OVERDUE and no outbound to him appears in mail or the text relay. Stated as ABSENCE, not failure: a phone call leaves no trace here.
🔥 WROTE THE OFFER. Contract, pre-approval letter and a personal letter from the buyers, submitted 3:15 PM, followed by his own text eleven minutes later.

oweFeedback.when: 🔴 ASKED THREE TIMES — Thu 7/30, Fri 7/31, Sat 8/1 — from the Keller Williams Realty Hoover listing side after your 7/30 tour, and you have since CLOSED on the property AND BEEN PAID. ⭐ STILL THE MOST OVERDUE ITEM ON THE BOARD in relationship terms, and getting paid sharpened it. Before the closing it read as an oversight; after completing a deal together and collecting on it, it reads as a shrug at the agent across the table. ⚠️ Their last request is now a week old and the listing has gone EXPIRED in their system — the window where feedback is still useful to them is closing. Thirty seconds, and the same message carries the two answers you actually want back.
